It also strengthens operational decision-making by providing earlier visibility of delivery and service-performance issues.

Philips continues to incur recurring upgrade costs, remains constrained by current platform limitations, increases future migration complexity, and delays consolidation of file-sharing services onto a modern cloud-ready architecture.

Name: Cloud File Share Solution (CFSS)
Before: Global
After:
CFSS is a replatforming initiative intended to replace the current Cache-based file-sharing solution used across 14 sites with a modern cloud-enabled file sharing architecture based on Nutanix Unified Storage (NUS) and PeerGFS technologies. The current platform has functional limitations and requires recurring upgrade activities that generate approximately $96K of upgrade-related costs during each major refresh cycle.

The proposed solution addresses scalability, synchronization, file-locking, resiliency, and operational constraints of the current environment while simplifying the storage landscape and providing a more sustainable long-term architecture. Scope includes solution design, platform deployment, migration activities, validation, performance testing, and rollout preparation across participating sites.

Name: Cloud File Share Solution (CFSS)
Before: eliminates recurring $96K upgrade costs and delivers $50K cloud savings per year across 14 sites
After:
Elimination of recurring Cache upgrade costs (~$96K).
Cloud infrastructure savings of approximately $50K per site. 
Reduced operational effort associated with distributed file-share management.
Simplification of the storage landscape across 14 locations.
Reduced technical debt and improved maintainability of the file-sharing platform.

The decommissioning component is the retirement of the existing Cache-based file-sharing platform following successful migration to the new architecture. Savings realization is contingent upon full migration completion and retirement of legacy infrastructure components supporting the current platform.

This demand covers Infrastructure Services activities required to support the global Real Estate portfolio, including new site openings, office relocations, site consolidations, expansions, and site closures. Scope includes campus networking (Cisco/Juniper LAN), WAN connectivity, NAC, micro-segmentation, wireless infrastructure, collaboration and meeting room technologies, AV/display equipment, equipment room setup, and associated implementation services. Infrastructure requirements are directly driven by Real Estate projects and must be delivered before site occupancy, business transition, or site closure can be completed.
The €2.5M request represents estimated 2027 project investments required to support the currently identified Real Estate portfolio across regions and is based on historical deployment patterns, expected site volumes, infrastructure refresh requirements, and infrastructure components required for new and relocated facilities. Cost estimates are intentionally high-level because detailed site designs become available only after Real Estate projects are formally approved.
This demand is categorized under Decommissioning/Replatforming, due to a significant portion of the investment enables retirement and removal of infrastructure assets associated with site closures and consolidations, avoidance of parallel infrastructure operations during relocations, and migration to modern network architectures incorporating NAC, micro-segmentation, and WAN modernization
Cost of not doing: Real Estate programs would be unable to execute site openings, closures, and relocations on time; regulatory, security, and operational requirements would not be met; and Philips would face project delays, business disruption, increased risk from legacy infrastructure, and potential duplicate operating costs during site transitions
